translations.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, an appointed apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
which he promised beforehand through his prophets in the holy scriptures
concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh,
who was shown to be the Son of God by power and by the Spirit of holiness, through the resurrection from the dead of Jesus Christ our Lord,
from whom we have received grace and apostleship, to bring all the Gentiles into obedience of faith for the sake of his name,
among whom you too are, the called of Jesus Christ,
to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called saints: grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ!
First, I give thanks to my God through Christ Jesus for all of you, because that faith of yours is proclaimed throughout the whole world.
For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, how unceasingly I make remembrance of you
always in my prayers, and I entreat that now at last I may perhaps be granted success, by the will of God, in coming to you,
for I long to see you, so that I may impart to you some spiritual grace for your strengthening.
And this is the mutual encouragement among you, through that faith in one another, yours and mine.

I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that many times I have wanted to come to you, and I have been hindered until now, so that I might have some fruit among you also, as among the other nations.
I am a debtor to Gentiles and to barbarians, to the wise and to the foolish.
And such is my eagerness, that I may bring the good news to you also who are in Rome.
For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, for it is the power of God for the salvation of everyone who believes, of the Jew first and then of the Gentile.
For the righteousness of God is revealed in it from faith to faith, as it is written: The righteous shall live by faith.
For the wrath of God is to be revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and falsehood of men, who held the truth in falsehood,
for the knowledge of God is manifest among them, for God himself revealed it to them.
For his invisible things, from the creation of the world, are seen and made known in the things that were made, as well as his eternal power and divinity, so that they should be without answer,
for they knew God and did not glorify him as God or give him thanks, but became vain in their thoughts, and their senseless heart was darkened.
They called themselves wise and went mad,
and they exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for the likeness of the image of corruptible man and of birds and four-footed animals and creeping things.
Therefore God gave them over to the lust of their hearts, to uncleanness and to the defiling of their bodies among themselves.
They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and honored and served created things and not the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
Therefore God gave them over to the passion of defilement, for their women exchanged the natural order for what is against nature.

Likewise their men also abandoned the natural order with women and burned in their lust for one another. Men with men did what is shameful, and the recompense that was due for their error they receive in one another.
And as they did not test God so as to hold him in knowledge, God gave them over to that untested mind, to do what is improper;
filled with all falsehood, fornication, wickedness, greed, evil; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil habits;
whisperers, evil-speakers, grievers of God, revilers, arrogant, insolent, inventors of evil, disobedient to fathers and mothers,
without understanding, disorderly, unloving, implacable, merciless;
who knew the judgment of God, that those who do such things are worthy of death; not only do they do this, but they also take pleasure in those who do them.
Therefore you have no answer to give, O man, every one of you who judges, for in that by which you judge your fellow, you condemn yourself, for you do the very same thing that you judge.
We know this, that the judgment of God is true concerning those who do such things.
Do you really think this, O man, you who judge those who do such things and do the same yourself: that you will escape the judgment of God?
Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and long-suffering? Do you not recognize that the kindness of God is leading you to repentance?
But by that hardness of yours and your unrepentant heart you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and of the revelation and righteous judgment of God,
who will repay each person according to his deeds:
to those who endure in good work, who seek eternal life — glory and honor and incorruption;
but to those who are of strife, and disobedient to the truth and obedient to falsehood — wrath and anger.
Affliction and distress upon every human soul that does evil, the Jew first and then the Gentile!
Glory and honor and peace to everyone who does good, the Jew first and then the Gentile!
For there is no partiality with God.
For those who have sinned without the law will also perish without the law, and those who have sinned within the law will also be judged by the law.
For it is not the hearers of the law who will be justified before God, but the doers of the law who will be justified.
For when Gentiles, who do not have the law, do the natural law, these, because they do not have the law, are a law to themselves:
they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their mind bearing witness together with them, and among one another their thoughts accusing or else defending them,
on that day when God will judge the hidden things of people, according to my gospel, through Jesus Christ.
If you are given the name of Jew, and rest upon the law, and boast in God,
and know his will, and discern what is better, and are taught by the law,
and trust yourself to be a guide to the blind, a light to those who are in darkness,
a teacher of the foolish, an instructor of infants, and you have in the law the form of knowledge and of truth,
You who teach your fellow, do you not teach yourself?
You who preach against stealing, you steal; you who say not to commit adultery, you commit adultery; you who abhor idols, you rob the sanctuary.
You who boast in the law, by your transgression of the law you dishonor God.
For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you, as it is written.
For circumcision is of benefit if you keep the law, but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
Now then, if the uncircumcised man keeps the righteousness of the law, will not his uncircumcision be counted as circumcision?
And the one who is by nature uncircumcised [?], who fulfills the law, will judge you, who with the letter and circumcision are a transgressor of the law!
For it is not the one who is outwardly a Jew, nor the one who is outwardly circumcised in the flesh,
but the one who is a Jew in secret and has circumcision of the heart by the Spirit, not by the letter, whose praise is not from men but from God.
What then is the advantage of the Jew, or what benefit is circumcision?
Much in every way. First of all, because they were entrusted with the words of God.
But what then? If some became unbelieving, will their unbelief nullify the faithfulness of God?
Let it not be! Let God alone be true and every man a liar, as it is written: That you may be justified in your word and prevail in your judgment.
If our falsehood accords with the righteousness of God, what shall we say? Is there falsehood with God, who sends his wrath? Am I speaking in human terms?
Let it not be! Otherwise, how would God judge the world?
If the truth of God has abounded through my falsehood to his glory, why am I still judged as a sinner?
And why not, as we are slandered and as some claim that we say, 'Let us do evil so that good may come to us'? The condemnation of such people is in the judgment.
What then? Are we better off? Not at all, for we have already charged Jews and Gentiles alike with all being under sin.
As it is written: There is no one righteous, not even one;
there is no one who understands, there is no one who seeks out God;
all have turned aside together and become useless; there is no one who does kindness, there is not even one.
Their throat is an opened grave; with their tongues they have deceived; the venom of asps is on their lips,
whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
Their feet are swift to shed blood;
destruction and misery are in their ways;
And the way of peace they have not known.
There is no fear of God before their eyes.
Now we know this: that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may be liable to the judgment of God,
for by the works of the law no flesh will be justified before him, for from the law comes the knowledge of sin.
But now, apart from the law, the righteousness of God has been revealed, attested by the law and the prophets;
the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, to all and upon all who believe, for there is no distinction;
for all have sinned and have fallen short of the glory of God,
but they are justified freely by his grace and through the redemption of Jesus Christ,
whom God prepared beforehand as a propitiation through his faith, by his blood, to show his righteousness through the forgiveness of former sins,
in the forbearance of God, to show his righteousness at this present time, so that he may be righteous and the justifier from the faith of Jesus.
Where then is that boasting? Has it been excluded? By what law? Of works? No, but by the law of faith.
For we speak of the justification of a person by faith, apart from the works of the law.
Or is God the God of the Jews only, and not of the Gentiles also? Yes, of the Gentiles also,
since God is one, who justifies the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised by that same faith.
Do we now nullify the law through that faith? Let it not be! Rather, we establish the law.
What then shall we say? Did Abraham, our father, find anything according to the flesh?
If Abraham was justified from works, he has a boast, but not before God.
For what does the scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
Now to the one who works, the wage is not counted as a favour but as a debt.
But the one who does not work, and believes in the one who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned to him as righteousness.
Just as David speaks of the blessedness of the person to whom God reckoned righteousness apart from work:
Blessed are those whose iniquities have been forgiven and whose sins have been covered;
blessed is the man to whom the Lord has not reckoned sin.
Now then, is this blessedness upon the circumcision, or upon the uncircumcision also? For we say that his faith was reckoned to Abraham as righteousness.
How then was it reckoned? Was he still in circumcision or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

And he received circumcision as a sign, a seal of the righteousness of the faith that he had in uncircumcision, so that he might be the father of all uncircumcised believers, so that it might be reckoned to them also as righteousness,
and father of the circumcision, not of the circumcised only, but also of those who stand in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had while uncircumcised.
For the promise to Abraham or to his descendants, that he would be heir of the world, did not come from the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
For if those who are of the law are the heirs, faith is empty and the promises are made void.
For the law brings about wrath, and where there is no law, there is no transgression of the law either.

For this reason it is from faith, so that the promise may be firm by grace for all the descendants, not only for those who are of the law, but also for those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all,
as it is written: "I have appointed you father of many nations," before the face of God, in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and ordains what does not exist as though it existed.
Beyond hope, he believed in hope that he would become the father of many nations, according to what was said: "So shall your descendants be."
And he did not grow weak in faith when he considered himself — for his flesh was nearly dead, since he was about a hundred years old — and the deadness of Sarah's womb.
But he did not waver in unbelief concerning the promise of God; rather, he grew strong in faith and gave glory to God,
and was fully convinced that he who had promised was also able to do it.
Therefore it was also reckoned to him as righteousness.
But it was not written for his sake alone that it was reckoned to him as righteousness,
but also for our sake, to whom it is to be reckoned, who believe in the one who raised our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead,
who was handed over for our sins and was raised for our justification.
Now therefore, since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
through whom we have also gained access by faith to this grace in which we stand, and we boast in the hope of the glory of God.
And not only this, but we also boast in afflictions, knowing that affliction produces endurance,
and endurance produces tested character, and tested character produces hope.
And hope does not put us to shame, for the love of God has been poured out in our hearts by the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.
For while we were still weak, Christ died for the ungodly at the appointed time.
For scarcely will anyone die for a righteous person, but for a good person — who knows — perhaps someone might even dare to face death.
But God has shown his own love toward us, for while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
How much more then, now that we are justified by his blood, shall we be saved by him from wrath.
If, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son, how much more, now that we have been reconciled, shall we be saved by his salvation!
And not only this, but we also boast in God through Jesus Christ our Lord, through whom we have now received this reconciliation.
Therefore, just as through that one man sin entered the world, and through sin, death, and so death came upon all people, by which all have sinned,
for until the coming of the Law sin was in the world, but it was not reckoned as sin at all without the Law.
Yet death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a type of the times to come.

But the grace is not like the trespass. For if by the trespass of that one man many perished, how much more have the grace of God and the gift by the grace of that one man Jesus Christ overflowed to many!
And the gift is not as it was through the one who trespassed, for the judgment from that one led to condemnation, but the grace, out of many trespasses, leads to justification.

For if by the trespass of that one man death reigned through that one, how much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and the gift of righteousness reign in life through that one, Jesus Christ!
Just as from the trespass of that one man it came upon all people for condemnation, so also because of the righteousness of that one man it came upon all people for justification of life.
For just as by the disobedience of that one man many entered as sinners, so also by the obedience of that one man many will enter as righteous.
For the Law came in between, so that sin might multiply; and where sin multiplied, there grace abounded all the more,
so that just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness for eternal life through Christ Jesus our Lord.
What then shall we say now? Shall we remain in sin so that grace may multiply? Let it not be!
We who have died by sin, how then shall we go on living in it?
Or do you not know that those of us who were baptized through Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
And we were buried together with him by that baptism into his death, so that just as Christ rose from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in renewal of life.
For if we have become planted together with him in the likeness of his death, so also shall we be in his resurrection.
We know this, that our old man was crucified with him, so that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, and so that we might no longer serve sin,
for he who has died has been justified from sin.
If we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him.
We know this, that Christ has risen from the dead and will die no more, and death will no longer have lordship over him.
For he who died, died by sin once; but he who lives, lives to God.
So you too, count yourselves dead on account of sin and alive to God through Christ Jesus our Lord.
Do not then let sin reign in those mortal bodies of yours, so that you obey it in its desires,
nor present those members of yours to sin as instruments of falsehood, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and those members of yours to God as instruments of righteousness.
And sin shall not have lordship over you, for you are not under the Law but under grace.
What then? Shall we go on sinning, because we are not under the law but under grace? May it not be!
Do you not know that to whomever you present yourselves as obedient slaves, you are the slaves of the one you obey, whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?
But thanks be to God, that you were slaves of sin, and you became obedient from the heart to the form of teaching to which you were handed over.
And now you have been set free from sin and have been enslaved to righteousness.

I speak in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh: just as you presented your members as slaves to impurity and lawlessness, unto lawlessness, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness, unto holiness.
For when you were slaves of sin, you were free from righteousness.
What fruit, then, did you have at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? For their end is death.
But now you have been set free from sin and enslaved to God, and you have your fruit unto holiness, and in the end, eternal life.
For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life through Christ Jesus our Lord.
Or do you not know, brothers, for I am speaking to those who know the law, that the law has authority over people for as long as a person lives?
For a married woman is bound by the law until the death of her husband; but if the husband dies, she is set free from the law of the husband.

So then, during her husband's lifetime she will be called an adulteress if she joins herself to another husband; but if her husband dies, she is free from that law, so that she is not an adulteress if she joins herself to another husband.
Therefore you too, my brothers, have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to him who was raised from the dead, in order that you may bear fruit for God.
For while we were in the flesh, the passions of sins, which came through the law, were at work in our members, so that we bore fruit for death.
But now we have been set free from the law and have died to that by which we were held captive, so that we may serve in a renewed spirit and not in an aged letter.
What then shall we say? Is the law sin? May it not be! But I would not have known sin except through the law. For I would not have known desire if the law had not said, "You shall not covet."
So sin found an occasion through the commandment and produced in me every desire, for without the law sin is dead.
I was once alive without the law, and when the commandment came, sin came to life,
and I died; and the commandment that was meant for life turned out for me to be for death.
For sin took occasion through the commandment, deceived me, and through it killed me.
Hence the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.

Did that good thing then become death for me? May it not be! Rather it was sin, so that sin might be shown to be sin through that good thing which became death for me, in order that sin might become exceedingly sinful through the commandment.
This we know, that the law is spiritual, and I am fleshly and reared in sin.
For what I do, I do not know; for I do not do what I want, but what I hate, that I do.
But if I do what I do not want, I bear witness together with the law that it is good.
Now therefore it is no longer I who do it, but the sin that dwells in me. 10 [?]
For I know that nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh; for the will is present with me, but I do not find how to do that good.
For I do not do the good that I want, but the evil that I do not want, that I do.
But if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but the sin that dwells in me.
Do I then find a law that would want me to do good, since evil is present with me?
For in the inner man I take pleasure together with the law of God.
And I see another law in my members, which opposes the law of my mind and takes me captive by the law of sin that is in my members.
Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me from this flesh of this death?
But I give thanks to God through Christ Jesus our Lord.
Is there, then, now any condemnation through Christ Jesus for those who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit?
For the law of the Spirit of life through Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and death.

For what was impossible for the law, in that it was weak because of the flesh, God did: he sent his Son in the likeness of the flesh of sin and on account of sin, and he condemned that sin by his flesh,
so that the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us, who conduct ourselves not in a fleshly way, but in a spiritual way.
For those who are fleshly think the things of the flesh, but those who are spiritual, the things of the Spirit.
For the thinking of the flesh is death, but the thinking of the Spirit is life and peace.
For the thinking of the flesh is enmity toward God, for it does not submit to the law of God, nor can it.
For those who are in the flesh cannot please God.
But you are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if the Spirit of God dwells in you. If anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to him.
If Christ is in you, let the flesh be dead because of sin, but the spirit alive because of righteousness.
If the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised Christ from the dead will also give life to that mortal flesh of yours through his Spirit that dwells in you.
Now therefore, brothers, we are under no obligation to the flesh, that you should live in a fleshly way.
For if you live in a fleshly way, you are going to die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the flesh, you will live.
For those who walk by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.
For you have not received the spirit of slavery, so as to be afraid again, but you have received the spirit of adoption, by which we cry out: Abba, Father!
The same Spirit bears witness to this spirit of ours that we are children of God.
And if children, then also heirs: heirs with God and joint heirs of Christ. If we suffer with him, we shall also be glorified with him.
For this is what I think: that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy of the glory to come, which is to be revealed toward us.
For the expectation of creation awaits the revelation of the children of God,
for creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but by him who subjected it, in hope,
that this creation itself also will be set free from slavery to corruption into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
We know that all creation groans together and travails together until now.
And not only it, but we ourselves also, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, we ourselves also groan within ourselves and await the adoption, the redemption of our bodies,
for we are saved by hope. But hope that is seen is not hope, for what someone sees, why would he still hope for it?
But we hope for what we do not see, for we wait with patience.
Likewise the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we do not know what we should pray for as is fitting; but the Spirit himself intercedes for us with wordless sighing.
And he who searches hearts knows what the thought of the Spirit is, for he intercedes before God for the saints.
This we know: that for those who love God, all things work out for good, for those who are appointed by his command.
For those whom he foreknew, he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, so that he might be the firstborn among many brothers;
and those whom he predestined, he also called; and those whom he called, he also justified; and those whom he justified, he also glorified.
What then shall we say to this? If God is on our side, who is the one doing evil to us?
He who did not spare even his own Son, but gave him up for us all, how then will he not with him grant us all things?
Who is the accuser of God's elect? God is the one who justifies.
And who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that, rose again; who is at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us.
Who will separate us from the love of Christ: affliction or distress, persecution or hunger, nakedness or anguish or the sword? As it is written:
For your sake we are being killed every day, and we are counted as sheep for slaughter.
But over all this we will prevail through him who loved us.
For I believe that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor this world, nor that world,
nor heights, nor depths, nor any other created thing will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is through Christ Jesus our Lord.
I speak the truth through Christ and do not lie, my mind bearing witness with me by the Holy Spirit,
that I have great sorrow and unceasing pain in my heart.
For I would pray that I myself be accursed from Christ for the sake of my brothers and my kindred according to the flesh,
who are the Israelites, to whom belonged the adoption and the glory and the covenants and the giving of the law and the services of worship and the promises;
to whom belonged the fathers, and from whom is Christ according to the flesh, who is God over all, blessed forever. Amen.
But it could not be that the word of God has fallen, for not all these who are from Israel are Israel,
nor are all the descendants of Abraham children, but: "From Isaac shall your seed be named."
That is to say, it is not these children of the flesh who are children of God, but the children of the promise are reckoned as seed.
For this word is from the promise: At just this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son.
And not only this, but Rebecca too had children from one bed, from Isaac our father;
for when they had not yet been born, nor had done anything good or evil — so that God's predetermination by election might stand,
not from works but from him who called — he said to her: The elder shall serve the younger.
As it is written: Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.
What then shall we say? Is there any falsehood with God? May it not be!
For thus he says to Moses: I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will show favor to whom I show favor.
So then it is not of the one who wills, nor of the one who runs, but of the one on whom God has mercy.
For the scripture says to Pharaoh: For this very reason I raised you up, that I might show my power in you and that my name might be proclaimed in all the earth.
So then he has mercy on whom he wills, and he hardens whom he wills.
Perhaps you will say to me: Why then does he still lay blame? For who has resisted his will?
So then, O man, who are you who answer back to God? Will the thing made say to its maker: Why did you make me like this?
Or does the potter not have power over the clay, to make from the same kneaded lump one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
What if God, wishing to show his wrath and make known his power, has endured with much long-suffering the vessels of wrath prepared for destruction,
and in order to show the riches of his glory upon the vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory,
even us, whom he called not only from among the Jews but also from among the gentiles?
As he says in Hosea: I will call what was not my people my people, and what was not my beloved beloved.
And it shall be that in the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, there they shall be called sons of the living God.
And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: Though the number of the sons of Israel be as the sand of the sea, only a remnant will be saved;
For a word accomplishing and cut short in righteousness, for the Lord will make a shortened word upon the earth.
And as Isaiah said beforehand: If the Lord Sabaoth had not left us a seed, we would have become like the Sodomites and would have been made like the Gomorrahites.
What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, attained righteousness, but the righteousness that is from faith.
But Israel, pursuing the law of righteousness, did not reach the law of righteousness.
Why? Because it was not from faith, but as if from the works of the law; for they stumbled on the stone of stumbling.
As it is written: Behold, I am laying in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; and everyone who believes in him will never be put to shame.
Brothers, the desire of my heart and my supplication to God for Israel is for their salvation.
I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not with knowledge.
For they were ignorant of the righteousness of God, and they sought to establish their own righteousness and did not submit to the righteousness of God,
for the end of the law is Christ, as savior of everyone who believes.
For Moses writes of the righteousness that is from the law, that: The man who does it will live by it.
But the righteousness from faith speaks thus: Do not say in your heart: Who will go up into heaven? That is, to bring Christ down.
Or: Who will go down into the abyss? That is, to bring Christ up from the dead.
But what does it say? Near you is that word, in your mouth and in your heart; that is, the word of faith that we preach,
that if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe with your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
For with the heart you believe unto righteousness, and with the mouth you confess unto salvation.
For the scripture says: Everyone who believes in him will never be put to shame.
For there is no distinction between Jew and Gentile, for he himself is Lord of all, who enriches all who call upon him.
For everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.
How then will they call upon him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe him whom they have not heard? Or how will they hear without preaching?
Or how will they preach unless someone sends them? As it is written: How beautiful are the feet of those who bring the good news of peace, who bring good news of good things!
But not all obeyed the gospel, for Isaiah says: Lord, who has believed our report?
So then faith indeed comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of God.
But I say: Did they perhaps not hear? But it says that: Their voice has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
But I say: Did Israel perhaps not understand? First Moses says: I will make you jealous over what is not a nation, and with a senseless nation I will make you angry.
But Isaiah dares to say: I was found by those who did not seek me, and I was revealed to those who did not ask for me.
But to Israel he says: All day long I have stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.
I say then: Has God perhaps cast away his people? May it not be! For I too am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not cast away his people, whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says of Elijah? How he appeals to God, accusing Israel:
Lord, they have slain your prophets and torn down your altars; and I alone am left, and they seek my life as well.
But what does the command of the word say to him? I have kept for myself seven thousand men whose knees have not bowed to Baal.
So then, now too, at this present time, a remnant has come to be by the election of grace.
But if it is by grace, it is no longer from works; otherwise grace is no longer reckoned as grace. But if it is from works, it is no longer grace [?], since work is no longer work.
What then? What Israel seeks, this it did not attain. But the elect attained it, and the others were blinded,
as it is written: God gave them a spirit of sorrow, eyes so that they should not see and ears so that they should not hear, down to this very day.
And David says: Let their table become before them a snare and a retribution and a stumbling block for them.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they do not see, and bend their back continually!
But I say: Did he perhaps make them stumble so that they should fall? May it not be! Rather, through their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make them jealous.
But if their trespass is the riches of the world, and their defeat the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fullness!
But I say to you, you Gentiles: inasmuch as I am an apostle of the Gentiles, I will glorify this ministry of mine,
if only I may make my own flesh jealous and save some of them.
For if their falling away is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be, if not life from the dead?
But if the firstfruit is holy, so also is the dough; and if the root is holy, so also are its branches.
But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive, were grafted in upon them and became a sharer in the root and richness of the olive,
do not boast over those branches. But if you do boast, it is not you who bear the root, but the root that bears you.
You will say then: The branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.
Good! They were broken off through their unbelief, but you stand through faith; do not be haughty, but be afraid!
If God did not spare the natural branches, perhaps he will not spare you either.
See then the kindness and the severity of God: severity toward those who fell, but kindness toward you, if you remain in that kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off.
And they too, if they do not remain in their unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

For if you were cut off from what is by nature a wild olive tree and, contrary to nature, were grafted onto the good olive tree, how much more will these, who are so by nature, be grafted onto their own olive tree!

I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, of this mystery, so that you may not be wise in your own eyes: that blindness has come upon Israel for a time, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in.
And in this way all Israel will be saved, as it is written: "The Deliverer will come from Zion and will turn Jacob from ungodliness."
"And this is my covenant with them, when I wipe away their sins."
With respect to the gospel they are enemies for your sake, but with respect to election they are beloved for the sake of the fathers.
For the gifts of grace and the callings of God are irrevocable.
For just as you too were once disobedient to God, but have now received mercy through their disobedience,
so these too have now become disobedient for the sake of the mercy shown to you, so that they too may receive mercy.
For God has confined all people in disobedience, so that he may have mercy on all.
O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments and how untraceable are his ways!
For who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?
Or who has first given anything to him, so that he should be repaid?
For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
I beseech you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, which is your rational service.
And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, so that you may discern what the will of God is: good, pleasing and perfect.

For by the grace of God that has been given to me I say to everyone who is among you: do not think more highly of yourself than is proper, but think with sober purity, each one according to the measure of faith that God has apportioned.
Just as in one body we have many members, but all the members do not have the same function,
so we all are one body in Christ, and individually we are members of one another.
And we have gifts that differ according to the grace given to us: whether prophecy, according to the measure of faith;
or whoever serves, in service; or whoever teaches, in teaching;
or whoever comforts, in comforting; whoever gives, with generosity; whoever presides, with diligence; whoever shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
With unfeigned love, shun evil and cling to what is good.
In brotherly love be tenderly devoted to one another; in showing honor outdo one another.
Do not be lazy in zeal; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord.
Rejoice in hope, endure in affliction, be diligent in prayer.
Share in the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality.
Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep.
And be of the same mind toward one another; do not set your mind on what is high, but associate with what is lowly; do not become wise in your own eyes.
And let none of you repay evil for evil; plan beforehand what is good in the sight of all people.
If it is possible on your part, keep peace with all people.
Do not seek vengeance by yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath, for it is written: "Vengeance is mine, and I will repay, says the Lord."
But if your enemy is hungry, give him bread; and if he is thirsty, give him drink; for by doing this you will gather coals of fire on his head.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
Let every person submit to the higher authority, for there is no authority except from God; and the authorities that exist are appointed by God.
Therefore whoever opposes the authority opposes the command of God. And those who oppose it will bring judgment on themselves.
For the rulers are not a terror to those who do good, but to those who do evil. Do you wish to have no fear of the authority? Do good, and you will receive praise from it,
for it is God's servant to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid, for it does not bear the sword in vain; for it is God's servant to you, an avenger for wrath against the one who does evil.
Therefore it is necessary to submit, not only because of wrath, but also for the sake of the scruple of conscience.
For this reason you also pay tribute, for they are servants of God, devoted to this very labor.
Give therefore to all what is owed: tribute to whom tribute is due, toll to whom toll is due, fear to whom fear is due, honor to whom honor is due.
Owe nothing to anyone except love for one another, for whoever loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law,

namely: You shall not commit adultery, you shall not kill, you shall not steal, you shall not covet; and whatever other commandment there is, it is fulfilled in this one word, namely: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
Love does no evil to its neighbor; the fulfiller of the law is love.
And know this about the time, that it is already the hour for us to awaken from sleep. For now salvation is nearer to us than when we first believed.
The night has moved far from us, and the day has drawn near to us; let us therefore put away the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.
And as in the daytime, let us walk becomingly, not in revelry and drunkenness, not in beds and defilement, not in strife and envy,
but put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make the thought of the flesh into lust.
And receive the one who is weak in faith, not with doubts and disputing thoughts.
One person believes he may eat everything, but the weak one eats vegetables.
Let the one who eats not despise the one who does not eat, and let the one who does not eat not judge the one who eats, for God has accepted him.
Who are you, that you judge another's servant? By his own lord he stands or falls; and he will indeed stand, for God is able to make him stand.
Some fast every other day, and some fast every day; let each one be fully satisfied in his own mind.

Whoever gives thought to the day gives thought to it for the Lord; and whoever does not give thought to the day, likewise for the Lord does not give thought to it. And whoever eats, eats for the Lord, and gives thanks to God; and whoever does not eat, likewise for the Lord does not eat, and gives thanks to God.
For none of us is alive by himself, and no one dies by himself.
For whether we live, we live for the Lord, and whether we die, we likewise die by the Lord; whether we are alive or whether we die, we are the Lord's.
For this reason also Christ died and rose and lived, so that he might be Lord over both the dead and the living.
But you, why do you judge your brother? Or you, why do you despise your brother? For we are all to stand before the judgment seats of Christ.
For it is written: "I live, says the Lord, for to me every knee shall bend, and every tongue shall confess to God."
So then each of us shall give an account of himself to God.
Let us no longer judge one another, but rather judge this: that you not place a stumbling block or an occasion of error before a brother.
I know and am persuaded by the Lord Jesus that nothing is defiled in itself; but if anyone regards something as defiled, that thing is defiled.
If your brother is grieved because of food, you are no longer walking in love. Do not by your food destroy him for whom Christ died.
So then let that good of yours not be reviled.
For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
For whoever serves Christ in these things is pleasing to God and approved by people.
So now let us pursue peace and the building up of one another.
Do not destroy the work of God for the sake of food. All things are pure, but it is evil for the person who eats so as to cause stumbling.
It is better not to eat meat, nor to drink wine, nor to do anything by which your brother stumbles, or is tripped up, or grows weak.
Do you have faith? Have it for yourself before God. Blessed is he who does not judge himself in what he is tested by.
But whoever doubts is condemned even if he eats, because he does not eat in faith; and everything that is not of faith is sin.
Now to him who is able to establish you according to my gospel and the preaching of Christ Jesus, by the revelation of the mystery that was kept silent in the ages of old,
but is now revealed through the prophetic scriptures, by the command of the eternal God, and made known to all the Gentiles for the obedience of faith,
to the only wise God, through Christ Jesus, whose is the glory forever and ever. Amen.
But we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the feeble, and not to please ourselves;
let each of us please his neighbor for his good, for building up.
For Christ too did not please himself, but as it is written: "The reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen upon me."
For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through patience and through the consolation of the Scriptures we may have hope.
And may the God of patience and consolation grant you to be of the same mind toward one another in regard to Christ Jesus,
so that together, with one mouth, you may glorify God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore receive one another, just as Christ received you, to the glory of God.
And I speak of Jesus Christ, for he became a servant of the circumcision for the sake of the truth of God, to confirm the promise made to the fathers,
and that the Gentiles, for the sake of mercy, might glorify God, as it is written: Therefore I will confess you among the Gentiles, Lord, and sing to your name.
And again it says: Rejoice, you Gentiles, with his people.
And again it says: Sing to the Lord, all you tribes, and praise him, all peoples.
And further Isaiah says: And there shall be the root of Jesse, he who is to rise up as ruler of the Gentiles; and in him the Gentiles will hope.
And may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope and in the power of the Holy Spirit.
I am convinced concerning you, my brothers, that you too are full of goodness and filled with all knowledge, and able also to teach one another.
I have written to you rather boldly, brothers, in part, in order to remind you, by the grace that has been given to me by God,
that I might be a servant of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, laboring as a priest in the gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles may be acceptable and sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
So I have a boast through Christ Jesus before God.
For I will not dare to speak of anything that Christ has not done through me to bring the Gentiles to obedience, by word and deed,
by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God, so that from Jerusalem and round about as far as Illyricum I might fulfill the gospel of Christ.
And thus I have been honored to preach the gospel, not where Christ has been named, so that I would not build on another's foundation,
but as it is written: Those to whom nothing has been told about him shall see, and those who have not heard shall understand.
For this reason also I have been hindered from coming to you.
But now I no longer have any place in these regions here, and I have longed for many years to come to you.
And if I go to Spain, I will come to you, for I hope that when I am going there I will see you too and be sent on my way there by you, if first I have been somewhat satisfied by seeing you.
But now, behold, I am going to Jerusalem to serve the saints.
For Macedonia and Achaia have resolved to make some contribution for the poor among the saints who are in Jerusalem.
They resolved to do so, and indeed they are their debtors. For if the Gentiles have come to share in their spiritual things, they ought also to serve them in bodily things.
So when I have completed this and have sealed this fruit of theirs for them, I will go on by way of you to Spain.
And this I know, that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ.
Now I beseech you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to become my fellow strivers in prayers to God on my behalf,
that I may be delivered from the disobedient in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be acceptable to the saints,
so that I may come to you with joy by the will of God and find rest with you.
And may the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is a servant of the church of the Cenchreans,
that you may receive her in the Lord as is worthy of the saints, and stand by her in whatever matter she may need from you; for she too has become a helper of many, and of me myself as well.
Give greetings to Priscilla and Aquila, my fellow helpers in Christ Jesus,
who stretched out their necks for my life, to whom not only I am grateful, but also all the churches of the Gentiles,
and greet the congregations in their houses. Give greetings to Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the firstfruit of Achaia for Christ.
Give greetings to Mary, who labored greatly for you.
Give greetings to Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and my fellow captives, who are distinguished among the apostles, who were also in Christ before me.
Give greetings to Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
Give greetings to Urbanus, our helper in Christ, and to Stachys, my beloved.
Give greetings to Apelles, chosen in Christ. Give greetings to those of the household of Aristobulus.
Give greetings to Herodion, my kinsman. Give greetings to those of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
Give greetings to Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who have labored in the Lord. Give greetings to Persis, the beloved, who labored greatly in the Lord.
Give greetings to Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and to his mother and mine.
Give greetings to Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them.
Give greetings to Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. The churches of Christ greet you.
I beseech you, brothers, beware of those who cause division and stumbling contrary to the teaching that you have learned, and keep away from them.
For such people do not serve our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly, and by their sweet speech and blessing they deceive the hearts of the innocent.
For your obedience is renowned among all; therefore I rejoice over you, and I want you to be wise as to what is good and innocent as to what is evil.
And may the God of peace crush the devil under your feet soon. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.
Timothy, my helper, greets you, and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen.
I, Tertius, who wrote this letter in the Lord, greet you.
Gaius, who is host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the steward of the city, greets you, and Quartus, the brother.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
